recipes.description: Scooped-mid Mesa Mark IIC+ style high-gain rhythm tone with a Tube Screamer in front to tighten the low end. The TS is set low-drive / high-tone — it acts as a clean boost, not a distortion source.
Marshall Plexi-style mid-gain rock rhythm. No pedals — the gain comes from the amp. Forward mids (Marshall signature), present but not bright treble, no modulation or delay.
Fender Tweed / Vibroverb-style blues with a Tube Screamer driving the front end. Mid-forward, fat bottom, light reverb. Lots of dynamics — the gain should clean up with the volume knob.
Soaring sustaining lead in the Gilmour mold: moderately driven amp, long sustain, prominent quarter-note-ish delay (~400ms feel) with moderate feedback, and a lush hall reverb behind everything.
Classic surf: bright Fender-style clean, drippy spring reverb, lush tremolo. No drive, no modulation other than tremolo. The reverb level should be obvious — surf is half guitar, half reverb.

aliases: where the streets have no name
recipes.description: Bright clean tone with a rhythmic dotted-eighth delay sitting prominently in the mix — the delay is part of the riff, not background flavor. Moderate hall reverb behind it. No drive.
Marshall stack pushed into a vintage fuzz pedal. The fuzz does most of the saturation, the amp adds warmth. Mids forward, no modulation, dry-ish room. Lift the gain knob and it should clean up.

aliases: studio clean with chorus and delay
recipes.description: Modern studio clean: bright but not piercing, subtle chorus for movement, gentle short delay for size, hall reverb behind. The effects should be felt, not heard prominently.
Metallica Black Album-era rhythm. Less scooped than Mark IIC+ Puppets — Bob Rock cleaned up the production. Tight bottom, present mids, no boost in front.
Pristine Metallica clean intro. Bright Roland JC-style clean with subtle chorus and a touch of delay. Used as the dynamic counterpoint to the high-gain payoff.
Iron Maiden gallop rhythm. Marshall JCM800 mid-gain — not scooped like thrash, but bright and articulate so the gallop pattern stays defined. Slight room reverb.
Iron Maiden twin-lead tone — Marshall pushed harder than the rhythm, slight quarter-note delay for thickness, hall reverb. Mids forward so harmonised lines stay distinct.
Dave Mustaine tight thrash rhythm — high gain with a clear midrange and aggressive treble. A boost in front keeps the picking attack defined.
Slayer brutal thrash — extremely scooped mids, max gain, T-SCREAM boost in front. Tight, percussive, no room for cleanliness.
Dimebag Darrell Randall solid-state aggression. Maxed gain, bright treble, forward upper mids. Tight palm mutes — no boost needed, the amp is doing it all.
Dimebag lead tone — same brutal rhythm voicing pushed harder, with quarter-note delay for sustain and a touch of harmonized chorus to thicken the upper register.
Iommi cranked Laney/Marshall — dark, mid-thick, moderate gain. Bass forward but not flubby, treble rolled back. Light room reverb.
Adam Jones rhythm — moderate gain Diezel/Marshall stack, dark and chunky, slight chorus for movement, big hall reverb. Bass forward, mids present.
Mastodon sludgy high-gain rhythm — thick bottom, mids present, gain high but not scooped. Slight room reverb, no modulation.
Meshuggah-style djent — surgically tight high-gain with a TS-style boost in front choking the low end. Aggressive treble, scooped mids, very little reverb.
Lamb of God modern metalcore rhythm — high gain Mesa/PRS rig, tight bottom, slight mid scoop, present treble. T-SCREAM boost optional but here on for the tightening.
Gojira heavy modern metal — high gain with a slightly darker voicing than typical djent, tight, percussive. Light room reverb, no modulation.
Generic djent fallback — tight, slightly scooped, T-SCREAM boost in front, very little reverb. Use when description mentions djent but no specific band.
Jimmy Page cranked Marshall plexi — mid-gain, slightly hairy, mids forward, no pedals. Light room reverb. The breakup comes from the amp, not a stomp.
Page lead — same plexi pushed harder, light delay for size, hall reverb. Treble forward for cutting solos, but with body in the bass.
Joe Perry mid-gain rock rhythm — Marshall with a hint of overdrive boost, slightly mid-forward, present treble. The sound of '70s American hard rock radio.
Brian May Vox AC30 / treble booster lead — chimey upper-mid forward voicing, moderate gain, light delay and hall reverb. The signature 'orchestra of guitars' tone.
Pete Townshend windmill power-chord rhythm. Hiwatt-style mid-gain, bright but not piercing, mids forward, no pedals. Light room reverb for some space.
Hotel California intro voicing — clean Fender with a touch of compression and chorus, hall reverb behind. Bright but not piercing.
Eagles twin-lead solo — Marshall-pushed lead, mid-forward, light delay and hall reverb. Sustaining but never compressed-sounding.
Keith Richards open-G tweed-y rhythm. Just-broken-up crunch, mids forward, no pedals, slight room reverb. Loose feel, ragged edge.
Clapton's Cream-era woman tone — neck pickup into a cranked Marshall, treble rolled off on the guitar, sustaining and vocal. Light room reverb.
Layla outro / Allman slide territory — slightly broken-up tweed lead with a tube-screamer push, room reverb. Sustaining but never overdriven into mush.
Boston layered arena-rock voicing — bright Marshall lead with light chorus and short slap delay. Smooth, polished, sustaining without being mushy.
Neal Schon polished arena lead — Marshall lead with mild compression, hall reverb, light delay. Glassy and sustaining without ever sounding compressed.
Slash signature lead — Marshall JCM800 pushed, Les Paul into the front. Thick mids, sustaining, light hall reverb. Not too much treble — the bridge humbucker handles that.
Southern rock triple-guitar rhythm — Marshall with light breakup, mids and bass forward, no pedals. Just enough room reverb to feel like a stage.
Free Bird outro — Marshall LEAD pushed, light delay, hall reverb. Mid-forward, sustaining lead with vocal mids.
B.B. King — semi-hollow into a Fender Twin / Lab Series clean amp. Almost no breakup. Compression smooths the attack, light room reverb.
Albert King Memphis Stax blues — Acoustic 270 / Quad Reverb clean with a touch of breakup, no boost. Mids forward, bright but not biting.
Beano-era Clapton Les Paul into JTM45 — mid-gain breakup, no boost needed, mids forward, very little reverb. The original British blues tone.
John Mayer Dumble-ish modern blues — clean-edge tweed with a low-drive Tube Screamer for sustain, hall reverb. Mid-forward, vocal, never harsh.
Gary Moore Les Paul into Marshall — sustaining vocal lead, moderate gain, light hall reverb. Lush and singing, never harsh.
Joe Bonamassa cranked-Marshall blues-rock lead — high-headroom mid-gain with a clean boost, mids forward, hall reverb behind. Always articulate, never compressed.
Derek Trucks SG-into-Fender slide lead — clean-edge breakup, no boost, mids forward, light room reverb. The slide does the work; the amp stays out of the way.
Robben Ford Dumble-style fusion-blues lead — clean-edge breakup with subtle compression, hall reverb. Sustaining but never compressed-sounding.
Chicago blues shuffle — Fender Bassman tweed broken up, no boost, mids forward, bright. Light room reverb.
Generic blues rhythm fallback — clean-edge tweed with a touch of compression, mids forward, light reverb. Works as a starting point for any blues description.
Generic blues lead fallback — tweed pushed with a TS, compressed, mids forward, light reverb. Defaults toward the SRV/Texas voicing.
Delta blues — acoustic-style clean voicing with a faint room reverb, no modulation, no drive. Picking dynamics carry the tone.
Nirvana grunge rhythm — Fender Mustang into a Mesa with a Boss DS-1 / Big Muff style overdrive. Loose mids, present treble, dynamics-driven (the verse is clean-ish, chorus blooms).
Nirvana clean verse with the signature watery chorus — Small Clone-style chorus, clean Fender voicing, slight room reverb.
Soundgarden drop-tuned grungy rhythm — Marshall pushed, distortion in front for added grit, dark and mid-rich, slight modulation in places. Light room reverb.
Pearl Jam mid-gain rhythm — Marshall-flavored with a touch of breakup, mids forward, light room. Not as dark as Soundgarden, not as ragged as Nirvana.
Jerry Cantrell dark mid-heavy grunge — Bogner / Soldano pushed, scooped slightly, drop tuned weight. Light room reverb, no modulation.
Foo Fighters mid-to-high gain rhythm — Mesa Boogie style with present mids, no scoop, tight bottom. Slight room reverb.
Green Day pop-punk rhythm — Marshall pushed, bright, mid-present, no boost. Loose feel, lots of upstroke energy.
Dean DeLeo big rock rhythm — Marshall pushed with a slight overdrive boost, mids forward, bright but rounded. Light room reverb.
NIN industrial-rhythm voicing — heavily distorted, scooped, percussive. Tight low end, plenty of grit, very little reverb.
Jonny Greenwood big-distortion alt rhythm — Fender Telecaster into a heavy Big-Muff-style fuzz on top of a clean amp. Aggressive, gated feel.
Muse high-energy fuzz-rhythm — Manson into a Diezel-style stack pushed hard, fuzz on top, mids forward. Tight, percussive, slight room.
QOTSA stoner-rock rhythm — Ampeg-into-Marshall style fuzzy mid-gain, slightly dark, mids present. Light room reverb.
Frusciante 60s Strat into Marshall clean — bright, airy, very subtle chorus, no drive. Just enough room reverb to breathe.
Arctic Monkeys mid-gain garage-indie rhythm — Marshall pushed, slight breakup, mids forward, drier than American grunge. Light room.
The Strokes lo-fi garage-indie rhythm — bright Tele into a small clean-edge combo with a slight drive, no modulation. Very dry.
Black Keys grimy blues-rock — clean amp pushed with a heavy fuzz, dark mids, lo-fi feel. Tiny room reverb.

recipes.description: Tame Impala woozy psychedelic clean — heavy chorus and short slap delay on a warm clean amp. Compressed feel, modulation does the work.
Mac DeMarco woozy vibrato-soaked clean — clean amp with vibrato modulation, warm and slightly detuned-feeling. Light room reverb.
Post-punk jangly rhythm — bright clean amp with delay and chorus, very chimey. Light room reverb. The clean cousin of The Edge's voicing.
MBV shoegaze wall of sound — heavy reverb-soaked fuzz with heavy tremolo on top. Blurred and overwhelming on purpose. Hall reverb maxed.
Slowdive dreamy shoegaze clean — clean amp with chorus and long ambient delay, hall reverb cranked. No drive — the texture comes from modulation and reverb.
Post-rock crescendo voicing — clean Strat into ambient delay and hall reverb, light overdrive that blooms with playing dynamics. The reverb is the instrument.
Wilco mid-gain americana — clean-edge tweed with light overdrive, mids forward, light room reverb. Warm and unfussed.
Billy Corgan stacked-fuzz wall — Marshall pushed with Big Muff on top, dense, layered, mids forward. Light room reverb.
Bright Telecaster twang — clean Fender-style amp with heavy compression for sustain and even attack, short slap-back delay, light room. The compressor is the secret to country twang.
Tweed-amp country rhythm with just enough grit to dig in — gain on the edge of breakup, no separate drive pedal, light slap-back, light room.
Modern country radio lead — clean preamp pushed slightly, light compression, generous delay for sustain and width, hall reverb behind. Sounds polished, not vintage.
Bright Telecaster session-style country lead with strong compression, edge-of-breakup gain, short delay for note ring-out. Articulate over loud.
Warm hollow-body jazz — clean preamp with treble rolled back, no drive, no modulation, very light room. The dark, woody tone of a thumb-picked Gibson L-5.
Pat Metheny-style warm fusion lead — clean preamp, subtle chorus for movement, generous delay for that signature spaciousness, hall reverb. Treble rolled back from sparkly into woody.
Larry Carlton smooth ES-335 fusion tone — gently driven tube amp, gain on the edge of breakup, mid-forward, light reverb. Cleans up beautifully with the volume knob.
John Scofield bitey fusion — moderately driven amp, mid-forward, light overdrive to give phrases bite without going full distortion. No modulation. Light room.
George Benson smooth jazz clean — bright Polytone-style clean tone with light compression, no other effects, very light room. Sounds clean enough to record direct.
Nile Rodgers tight Strat funk — bright clean tone with HEAVY compression for the percussive 'chuck'. No drive, no modulation, almost no reverb. Compression IS the funk tone.
John Frusciante's funky Strat rhythm — slight crunch on the amp, compression on hard, no other effects. Stratty quack with a touch of grit.
Steve Cropper / Stax Records soul rhythm — clean Fender amp, light compression, no other effects. Dry, percussive, supportive — the guitar is the rhythm section.
Prince's percussive clean funk rhythm — bright clean amp, heavy compression, optional light chorus for shimmer, light reverb. Tight and intentional.
Modern worship pad-style clean — clean preamp, long delay layered with hall reverb to create a pad-like wash. The guitar disappears into the mix and becomes texture.
Modern worship soaring lead — moderately driven amp, plenty of compression for sustain, long delay and hall reverb for size. Anthemic, never aggressive.
Approximation of an acoustic fingerstyle tone using the AC preamp — flat EQ, slight compression for note balance, light room. Use the ME-80's AC preamp here, not CLEAN.

Bright arpeggiated clean for ambient or worship intros — clean preamp with treble pushed, light chorus for shimmer, moderate delay, big hall reverb. Cleaner than shoegaze, less effected than post-rock.
Dick Dale's fast tremolo-picked surf lead — clean Fender amp, drenched in spring reverb, no other effects. The reverb is half the sound.
The Ventures classic 60s instrumental rhythm — clean Fender, gentle tremolo from MOD, spring reverb at a reasonable level. Sounds like sunshine through a car radio.
Joe Satriani's melodic instrumental lead — moderate gain, mid-forward, light delay, generous hall reverb. Singing sustain without going metal.
Steve Vai's high-gain virtuoso instrumental lead — push the gain higher than Satch, brighter, longer delay tails, more reverb. Designed to sing across 8-bar phrases.
Generic country-style fallback when no specific song/artist matches. Bright clean tone with strong compression and short slap-back — covers the broad country territory.
Generic warm jazz fallback — clean preamp with treble rolled back, light compression, no effects except a touch of room. Woody, intimate, dark.
Generic funk fallback — bright clean tone with HEAVY compression, no drive, almost no reverb. The compressor IS the funk sound.
Generic modern worship fallback — clean preamp, light compression, generous delay and hall reverb stacked for pad-like ambience.
Generic ambient volume-swell fallback — clean preamp, comp for even volume, long delay and big hall reverb for the wash. Use a volume pedal or fingers to swell into chords.
